facts.fact: Section 194P of the Income Tax Act, 1961 sets the conditions under which senior citizens aged 75 or above are exempt from filing a return; condition 1: age 75 years or above
facts.quote: Section 194P of the Income Tax Act, 1961 provides conditions for exempting Senior Citizens from filing income tax returns aged 75 years and above. Conditions for exemption are: Senior Citizen should be of age 75 years or above

facts.fact: Condition: the senior citizen must be resident in the previous year
facts.quote: Senior Citizen should be of age 75 years or above Senior Citizen should be ‘Resident’ in the previous year

facts.fact: Condition: the only income is pension income and interest income (other income takes the person out of the exemption)
facts.quote: Senior Citizen has pension income and interest income only & interest income accrued / earned from the same specified bank in which he is receiving his pension
facts.note: Derived: the quote's condition is pension and interest income only, so any other income fails it.

facts.fact: Condition: the interest is earned from the same specified bank in which the pension is received (interest from another bank or the post office does not qualify)
facts.quote: Senior Citizen has pension income and interest income only & interest income accrued / earned from the same specified bank in which he is receiving his pension
facts.note: Derived: the condition is interest from the same specified bank that pays the pension, so interest from another bank or the post office does not meet it.

facts.fact: Condition: the senior citizen submits a declaration to the specified bank
facts.quote: The senior citizen will submit a declaration to the specified bank. The bank is a ‘specified bank’ as notified by the Central Government.

facts.fact: The specified bank computes and deducts the tax after the Chapter VI-A deductions and the section 87A rebate
facts.quote: Such banks will be responsible for the TDS deduction of senior citizens after considering the deductions under Chapter VI-A and rebate under Section 87A of Income Tax Act,1961.

facts.fact: Once the specified bank deducts the tax, the senior citizen (75+) need not file an income tax return
facts.quote: Once the specified bank, as mentioned above, deducts tax for senior citizens above 75 years of age, there will be no requirement to furnish income tax returns by senior citizens.

facts.fact: Otherwise the normal rule applies: an individual must file if total income before Chapter VI-A deductions exceeds the maximum amount not chargeable to tax (basic exemption limit)
facts.quote: Every individual whose total income before allowing deductions under Chapter VI‐A of the Income‐tax Act or deduction for capital gains (section 54 to 54GB), exceeds the maximum amount which is not chargeable to income‐tax is obligated to furnish his return of income.

facts.fact: For AY 2026-27, for ages 60 to 80 income up to Rs 3,00,000 is tax-free in the old regime and up to Rs 4,00,000 in the new regime
facts.quote: 60 years or more but less than 80 years of age anytime during the previous year are as under: Old Tax Regime New Tax Regime u/s 115BAC of the Income Tax Act,1961 Income Tax Slab Income Tax Rate Income Tax Slab Income Tax Rate Up to ₹ 3,00,000 Nil Up to ₹ 4,00,000 Nil
facts.note: AY 2026-27 is from the same page's heading ('Senior Citizens and Super Senior Citizens for AY 2026-2027', 'Tax Slabs for AY 2026-27').

facts.fact: From Tax Year 2026-27 the equivalent provision is section 393(1) [Table Sl. No. 8(iii)] of the Income-tax Act, 2025, and the declaration to the specified bank is made in Form No. 125 (rule 208, Income-tax Rules 2026)
facts.quote: The declaration under section 402(39)(c) read with section 393 (1) [Table: Sl. No. 8(iii)], may be furnished by the specified senior citizen to the specified bank in Form No. 125.

facts.note: Stated only on incometaxindia.gov.in (Form 125 FAQ / forms navigator: 'Form 125 (Earlier Form No. 12BBA)'), which blocks the page checker (HTTP 403); no incometax.gov.in or PIB page found that maps Form 125 to 12BBA. Retried in the audit on 28 Oct 2026: still HTTP 403.

summary: All 194P conditions, the bank TDS mechanism, the 60-80 slabs and the 2025 Act / Form 125 provision confirmed on incometax.gov.in pages; the 'old Form 12BBA' mapping is only on incometaxindia.gov.in (manual).
